subject: Energy
title: Hydrogen Pipelines and Transport
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Hydrogen Pipelines and Transport.

hook.text: Moving hydrogen from where it's made to where it's used is a huge challenge—it's the lightest molecule in existence.

buildup.text: Hydrogen can embrittle steel pipes—some existing gas pipelines can carry 20% hydrogen blends, but not pure H₂.

discovery.text: New hydrogen-rated pipelines are being planned across Europe—like the EU Hydrogen Backbone spanning 28,000 km.

twist.text: Shipping hydrogen overseas may be easier as ammonia—convert it, ship it, then crack it back to H₂ at the destination.

climax.text: Australia plans to export green hydrogen to Japan and Korea—shipping sunshine from the outback to Asian industry.

punchline.text: Hard to move, light as air—hydrogen logistics is half the battle.

quiz.question: Why can't most existing gas pipelines carry pure hydrogen?
